haiku-low.q1: A business event published to the domain-events topic by the existing outbox-relay. The Dispatcher consumes it and turns it into delivery rows.
haiku-low.q2: The Dispatcher inserts one deliveries row per matching active subscription. The unique key on (event_id, subscription_id) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING stops a redelivered copy creating a second row.
haiku-low.q3: It covers t.body, the timestamp plus the exact stored body, signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the subscription secret. It is recomputed on every attempt, including replays, with a fresh t.
haiku-low.q4: 2xx marks delivered. 410 marks dead (gone) and disables the subscription. Other 4xx marks dead (client_error). 408, 429, 5xx, timeouts and connection errors retry until attempt 8, then dead (retries_exhausted).
haiku-low.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second fails.
haiku-low.q6: In the deliveries table in the service's own Postgres: status, attempt_count, next_attempt_at, last_status_code and last_error.
haiku-low.q7: It waits as a pending row in deliveries with next_attempt_at set. Workers poll deliveries every 1 s and claim rows that are due, so the queue is not involved.
haiku-low.q8: The row stays sending. After lease_until (claim time plus 60 s) passes, the next poll by any worker reclaims it. The lost attempt counts toward the 8.
haiku-low.q9: Dead-lettered deliveries are the deliveries rows with status=dead. A replay sets status=pending, attempt_count=0 and next_attempt_at=now, keeping the same delivery id.
haiku-low.q10: The X-Webhook-Id header, which carries the delivery id. The receiver dedupes on it. It does not change between retries or after a replay.
haiku-low.q11: Rows already waiting are dead-lettered with reason subscription_disabled at their next claim, with no HTTP call.
haiku-low.q12: Yes. There is no ordering guarantee, because each delivery retries on its own schedule.

sonnet.q1: A message on the `domain-events` topic; the existing outbox relay publishes it, and the Dispatcher consumes it.
sonnet.q2: The Dispatcher reads active webhook_subscriptions matching the event's account_id and event_type (or '*') and inserts one deliveries row per match in one transaction. The unique key (event_id, subscription_id) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING means a redelivered or duplicate message creates no second row.
sonnet.q3: The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `t.body` (timestamp, a dot, and the stored body bytes) using the subscription secret. It is recomputed on every attempt, replays included, with a fresh `t`; the body itself is stored once.
sonnet.q4: 2xx: status=delivered. 410: dead (dead_reason=gone) and the subscription is disabled (disabled_reason=gone). Other 4xx: dead with dead_reason=client_error. 408, 429, 5xx, timeout, connection error: retried with backoff (pending, next_attempt_at set), or dead with retries_exhausted if attempt_count is 8.
sonnet.q5: At most 8 attempts (replay resets attempt_count to 0, so a replay starts a new set). The wait before attempt 3 is 2 minutes.
sonnet.q6: All in the `deliveries` table in the service's own Postgres: status, attempt_count, next_attempt_at (and lease_until), last_status_code and last_error.
sonnet.q7: It waits as a row in `deliveries` with status=pending and next_attempt_at set to the future time. The workers' poll (every 1 s, claiming due rows) picks it up when due; the queue is not used for retries.
sonnet.q8: The row stays `sending`. After lease_until (claim time + 60 s) passes, the next poll by any worker reclaims it and retries. The lost attempt counts toward the 8 because attempt_count was raised at claim time. The receiver may see the request twice and dedupes on X-Webhook-Id.
sonnet.q9: They are held in the `deliveries` table as rows with status=dead (deleted by the nightly job 14 days after dead_at). Replay sets status=pending, attempt_count=0, next_attempt_at=now, keeping the same delivery id.
sonnet.q10: The `X-Webhook-Id` header, which is the delivery id. It does not change between retries or after a replay (same delivery id).
sonnet.q11: At their next claim they are marked dead with dead_reason=subscription_disabled, without any HTTP call. The admin API refuses (409) to replay into a disabled subscription.
sonnet.q12: Yes. There is no ordering; each delivery retries on its own schedule, so a later event can arrive before an earlier one.
